questions.q: Why can't colon notation alone turn a JSON array field into multiple rows?
options: Colon notation returns the entire array as a single VARIANT value, not one row per element
Colon notation only works on numbers, never on arrays
Colon notation deletes arrays automatically
Snowflake doesn't allow arrays inside VARIANT columns at all
questions.explain: v:line_items returns the whole array as one value; it doesn't split it into rows. That's exactly the gap FLATTEN fills.

questions.q: What does the FLATTEN function do?
options: A table function that takes a VARIANT array as input and returns one row per array element
It converts a VARIANT column into a VARCHAR column
It deletes duplicate rows from a table
It compresses a table to save storage
questions.explain: FLATTEN is a table function — array in, one row per element out.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the LATERAL keyword in `LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v:line_items)`?
options: It lets FLATTEN reference the current row's other columns, so the parent record's fields stay attached to each flattened row
It sorts the flattened results alphabetically
It's required only when flattening numeric arrays
It converts the flattened rows back into a single VARIANT value
questions.explain: LATERAL allows FLATTEN to see and carry forward the other columns from the row being flattened — e.g. order_id and customer alongside each line item.

questions.q: In `LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v:line_items) AS item`, what does `item.value` refer to?
options: The flattened array element itself
The array's total length
The name of the VARIANT column being flattened
The row number of the parent record
questions.explain: item.value is the actual flattened element — you then use colon notation on it, like item.value:sku::string, to pull out its fields.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when should you use FLATTEN instead of the colon/dot notation from the previous lesson?
options: When a field is an array and you need one output row per array element
Always — colon notation should never be used once FLATTEN is available
Only when working with CSV files, never JSON
FLATTEN and colon notation are interchangeable in every situation
questions.explain: If every field you need is a scalar value, colon/dot notation is simpler. FLATTEN is specifically for turning an array field into multiple rows.
